raw_note:
1432 58yo M amb to triage c/o CP x2h, 7/10 pressure, rad to L arm, +diaphoretic, +nausea. A&Ox4, skin pale/clammy. NKDA. Hx HTN, HLD. Took ASA 81 at home.
VS: BP 164/96, HR 108, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA, T 98.4, pain 7/10.
1436 EKG done, ST elev II III aVF. Dr notified, at bedside. STEMI alert called.
18g R AC, 20g L FA, labs drawn (trop, BMP, CBC, coags). 2L NC, SpO2 now 98%. Cont monitor, NSR w/ occ PVCs.
ASA 324 chewed, NTG 0.4 SL x1, pain down to 4/10, BP 148/88. Pt denies SOB, no new c/o.
1450 cath lab accepted, transport at bedside. Wife present, updated. Report given to cath RN.
golden_note:
S (Subjective)
58 year old male reports chest pain for 2 hours, described as pressure, 7/10, radiating to the left arm, with nausea. History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia. No known drug allergies. Took aspirin 81 mg at home.

O (Objective)
1432: Ambulatory to triage. Alert and oriented x4. Skin pale, clammy and diaphoretic. BP 164/96, HR 108, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air, temperature 98.4 F, pain 7/10.
1436: EKG shows ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF.
Cardiac monitor shows normal sinus rhythm with occasional PVCs.

A (Assessment)
Chest pain with ST elevation on EKG.

P (Plan)
Transfer to cath lab. Continuous cardiac monitoring.

I (Intervention)
1436: Physician notified and at bedside. STEMI alert called.
IV access: 18 gauge right antecubital, 20 gauge left forearm. Labs drawn: troponin, BMP, CBC, coagulation studies. Oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula. Aspirin 324 mg chewed. Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual x1.
1450: Cath lab accepted, transport at bedside. Report given to cath lab RN. Wife present and updated.

E (Evaluation)
SpO2 improved to 98% on 2 L nasal cannula. After aspirin and nitroglycerin, pain decreased to 4/10 and BP to 148/88. Patient denies shortness of breath, no new complaints.

1436: Physician notified and at bedside. STEMI alert called.
IV access: 18 gauge right antecubital, 20 gauge left forearm. Labs drawn: troponin, BMP, CBC, coagulation studies. Oxygen 2 L by nasal cannula. Aspirin 324 mg chewed. Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg sublingual x1. Morphine 4 mg IV given.
1450: Cath lab accepted, transport at bedside. Report given to cath lab RN. Wife present and updated.

E (Evaluation)

S (Subjective)
Patient is a 58 year old man with 2 hours of chest pain that feels like pressure, rated 7 out of 10 and spreading down his left arm. He also feels nauseated. Past history includes high blood pressure and high cholesterol. He has no known drug allergies. He took aspirin 81 mg at home before coming in.

O (Objective)
Walked into triage at 1432. Alert and oriented x4. His skin is pale and clammy, and he is sweating. Initial vitals were blood pressure 164/96, heart rate 108, respiratory rate 22, oxygen saturation 94% on room air, temperature 98.4 F and pain 7/10.
At 1436 the EKG showed ST segment elevation in II, III and aVF.
The monitor shows normal sinus rhythm with occasional premature ventricular contractions.

A (Assessment)
Chest pain with ST segment elevation on the EKG.

P (Plan)
Continuous cardiac monitoring and transfer to the cath lab.

I (Intervention)
The physician was notified at 1436 and came to the bedside, and a STEMI alert was activated. Two IVs were placed, an 18 gauge in the right antecubital and a 20 gauge in the left forearm. Blood was drawn for troponin, BMP, CBC and coagulation studies. Oxygen started at 2 L via nasal cannula. Patient chewed aspirin 324 mg and received one sublingual nitroglycerin 0.4 mg.
At 1450 the cath lab accepted the patient and transport arrived at the bedside. Handoff report was given to the cath lab nurse. His wife is present and was updated.

E (Evaluation)
Oxygen saturation rose to 98% on 2 L nasal cannula. After the aspirin and nitroglycerin, pain eased to 4/10 and blood pressure came down to 148/88. He denies shortness of breath and has no new complaints.
